title: Drinking and nerves among performers; Leo throws things from the window
summary: Bunn says performers drank to face the stage, with stage fright; Leo got drunk on gin and threw things out a seventh-floor window.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: He was a nice person. He liked to drink a lot, though. Didn't they all at that time?
It seems like that keeps coming up, you know, as we talk about different people.
Yeah. I think that's what spoiled a lot of people.
Why do you think, you think because of the pressures or --
Well, it's pressures, yeah. When a man knows that he's got to go and do a set, he gets full of that whiskey, to hold the night out.
You mean because of stage fright or because of --
Not only stage fright. I mean, at least you get a little bit of it, but you know when you got to go on you go on and do that show.
Yeah.
But it's a funny feeling. I'll tell you that, because I know.
Yeah, I know too. I just --
You know too, don't you.
Sure.
When it's your time comes up that you've got to do your act. Sure it's a funny feeling.
But I've always found that I can function better, you know, straight, myself, you know. After you get past the first couple tunes, you know.
Yeah. Then you go on your own.
Then the music is what carries you.

Yes. Because, man, I used to suffer trying to wait to go on. And just the time you get to go on, boy, that's when it comes down harder. Knowing you've got to go on and it won't be but a couple of minutes before you go on.
Uh-huh.
That's the sad part of it. And the hurting part.
You mean that feeling that now you can't get out of it, right?
That's right.
It's going to happen whatever you do.
That's right. You've got to do it, in
order to keep your name up. You've got to do it. And I'd be looking like the devil, going out there and don't know what my name is.
(Laughter)
So you think a lot of the drinking came just from --
From that.
But what about the life itself? In other words --
The same thing. That's the attitude.
In other words, I mean if you -- people were playing a lot, I mean in speakeasies, and it was a drinking environment.
Problem, yeah.
Yeah. No, I mean everybody was drinking.
Yeah. It was a drinking problem.
Yeah.
Everybody done it. And mostly the actors.
Uh-huh.
The performers. Because they had to drink up a quart of whiskey before they'd go on the stage. A lot of them. God rest his soul, like Leo, got drunk off of gin.
Yeah.
And throwed our that stuff out the window.
Yeah.

Now, you wonder how the heck we think he felt. Think I never been that way, I took off all my clothes on the bare floor and laid down. I done that, I know that. But that cold felt -- that floor felt good to me.
Yeah, I can imagine that.
Here I am And burning up, and I laid on that cold floor.
Where was that, anyway?
Huh?
Do you remember where that was?
Do I remember where that was?
Yeah, that that happened.
Yeah, in New York.
Uh-huh.
Yeah. Right on 7th Avenue. God rest his soul, Leo threw things out the window. Seventh floor. He was so drunk off of gin. At a party we played in Florida.
I've always been amazed that his sense of pitch never went off, you know? To drink that much and be right on the money.
Uh-huh, all the time.
Yeah. It's amazing.
He wouldn't miss. God rest his soul.
And you know, he died out here?
